baselines: Random register pair submission (expected to fail leakage_detection_accuracy).

metrics.description: Binary metric: 1 if the correct leaking register pair is identified, 0 otherwise.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Binary metric: 1 if the report correctly identifies the alignment condition and second-order leakage, 0 otherwise.
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Binary metric: 1 if the report correctly states that both registers are safe under first-order analysis, 0 otherwise.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

acceptance_criteria: The submitted vulnerability_report.json passes all functional requirements (FR1-FR4).
The submitted vulnerability_report.json satisfies all security requirements (SR1-SR3).
A naive/empty submission (e.g., empty JSON object or missing fields) must fail evaluation.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: share0_stage2_q and share1_stage2_q are updated in the same cycle and their joint transition correlates with the unmasked value; retiming one share breaks the alignment.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Exact string match against the ground truth register names in the "leaking_register_pair" array.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify the pair (share0_stage2_q, share1_stage2_q) as the leaking register pair.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that the "first_order_analysis" array contains entries for both registers with "safe": true.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must state that both registers appear safe under individual first-order Hamming-distance analysis.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that the "alignment_condition" field contains a description matching the ground truth temporal alignment, and that "second_order_analysis.leaking" is true.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify that the joint transition leaks when both registers update in the same clock cycle.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker combines two centered power samples to cancel masking randomness and recover a secret-dependent intermediate.

constraints: The RTL contains a two-share masked datapath with multiple pipeline stages.
The leakage_models.json file defines both first-order and pairwise Hamming-distance leakage models.
The analysis must consider temporal alignment of register updates.
The submitted report must be self-contained and reference only the provided input artifacts.
expected_outputs: A vulnerability_report.json file identifying the leaking register pair and explaining the alignment condition.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted vulnerability_report.json must be valid JSON and parse without errors.
The report must identify exactly one leaking register pair in the "leaking_register_pair" field, and both names must match signal names present in the provided RTL.
The "first_order_analysis" array must contain entries for at least the two registers in the leaking pair, each with a boolean "safe" field.
The "second_order_analysis" object must contain a boolean "leaking" field and a non-empty "explanation" string.

public_spec.interface: The participant must submit a single file named vulnerability_report.json in the submission/ directory. The file must conform to the schema defined in response_format.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided two-share masked datapath RTL and identify a pair of share registers whose combined transitions leak information about the unmasked value, even though each register appears safe under individual first-order analysis.
public_spec.response_format:
The submission file vulnerability_report.json must be a JSON object with the following required fields:
- "leaking_register_pair": an array of exactly two strings, each being the hierarchical signal name of a register (e.g., "top.u_dut.share0_stage2_q").
- "alignment_condition": a string describing the temporal condition under which the joint transition leaks (e.g., "both registers update on the same clock cycle").
- "first_order_analysis": an array of objects, each with fields "register" (string) and "safe" (boolean), indicating whether the register appears safe under individual first-order Hamming-distance analysis.
- "second_order_analysis": an object with fields "leaking" (boolean) and "explanation" (string).
